text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 20: With a calendar baseline, the fitted solar capacity of the 25 BMUs is 1,160 MW with no battery and 1,154 MW with a 200 MW battery, against the solar study's 1,089 MW and 1,163 MW'
text.tspan: Figure 20: With a calendar baseline, the fitted solar capacity of the 25
BMUs is 1,160 MW with no battery and 1,154 MW with a 200 MW battery,
against the solar study's 1,089 MW and 1,163 MW

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Sum of the fitted AC capacity of the four fleet curves (regional CAMS sky), with a seasonal calendar baseline and a battery of the assumed power and 2 hours of energy, fitted to half-hourly levels. The grey line is the same fit to each BMU's calendar replica, which has no cloud, so solar fitted there could be shape alone (all 25 BMUs: 216 MW with no battery and 426 MW at 200 MW). The blue lines are the solar study's totals over the same BMUs. No ground truth exists. The horizontal axis is stretched near 0.'
text.tspan: Sum of the fitted AC capacity of the four fleet curves (regional CAMS sky), with a seasonal calendar baseline and a
battery of the assumed power and 2 hours of energy, fitted to half-hourly levels. The grey line is the same fit to
each BMU's calendar replica, which has no cloud, so solar fitted there could be shape alone (all 25 BMUs: 216 MW
with no battery and 426 MW at 200 MW). The blue lines are the solar study's totals over the same BMUs. No ground
truth exists. The horizontal axis is stretched near 0.
